title: The charity hospital that pays like a bank
question: Do the nonprofit hospitals with the highest executive pay give the least charity care?
side_a: HEALTH__HOSPITAL_OFFICER_PAY - named officer, title, hours, total pay, from the 990
side_b: HEALTH__FED_CMS_HCRIS - charity care dollars, margin, assets, per fiscal year
side_c: HEALTH__FED_CMS_HOSPITAL_COMPARE - star rating
joins_on: EIN for the 990 side, CCN for the Medicare side
key_strength: EIN steel 86-100%; the EIN-to-CCN hop is the risk
a_hit_means: A hospital paying a CEO millions while writing off almost nothing is on the record, by name
a_miss_means: Pay tracks size, not stinginess, and the nonprofit label survives
visual: scatter, pay per hour against charity care share, one dot per hospital
story: Two filings that never meet: the tax form says what he earns, the Medicare report says what she gave away

title: Paid by the sponsor, running the trial

side_c: HEALTH__FED_CMS_NPPES - name to NPI so the investigator resolves
joins_on: NPI once the investigator name resolves
key_strength: NPI steel 100%; investigator name to NPI is the weak hop
a_hit_means: The person testing the drug was being paid by its maker in the same year
a_miss_means: Investigators are paid after, not during, and the timing defence holds
visual: timeline per trial, payment bars under the trial bar, one row per investigator
story: FDA registry and CMS payments are two agencies with no reason to talk

title: Who drinks from the failing pipe

story: EPA tracks the pipe, CMS and HUD track the people, nobody joins them
